conclusion.summary: Single buffering helps one fixed attention tile but does not beat the best baseline among the provider configurations on this workload. Keep options disabled by default.

scope: Unchanged real Tritonbench source, fixed configurations; bypassed provider autotuning and ordinary JIT argument specialization. The screen covers the exact provider tile/stage/warp grid, not the complete live provider execution path.

enable_aref_release_scheduling.effect: Run existing ownership-checked pass before Aref lowering; diagnostics only modify reporting.

enable_tmem_single_buffer.effect: Apply existing disallow_acc_multi_buffer policy before latency inference on marked Blackwell WS for loops; skip scopes with direct or nested explicit loop latencies.

screen.failures: Four stage-four BN128 configurations exceed shared-memory limits in both variants; no candidate-only failures.

measurement_notes: Timing comparisons use warmed synchronized interleaved CUDA graphs.
Identical PTX timing differences are noise controls, never compiler gains.
n_spills reports local memory bytes divided by four in this driver; it is not an executed spill-instruction count.
Hardware occupancy counters were not measured. Dynamic register redistribution prevents inferring occupancy from maxnreg alone.
Earlier blocked-environment and failed harness attempts are preserved as historical records.
next_step: Select real kernels whose best configurations are TMEM-limited after checking shared/register/local-memory/grid constraints. Explore partial reuse that preserves double-buffer overlap; attention P/QK reuse requires coupled slot mapping and PV read-completion before overwrite.

measurements.interpretation: All generated PTX is identical; no compiler speedup established
